application_guidance.input_pattern: Nonconvex finite sums with complete exact component p-jets and no lower-order derivative budget.

sensitive_conditions: Values and unrestricted model computation are substantive permissions.
A Hessian-only, tensor-vector or full-objective oracle has different resources.
Do not use this theorem as a second-order stationarity rate.

complexity_scope.guarantee: Minimax definition uses success >=2/3 per instance and deterministic query cap; upper construction achieves >=31/32 with an all-path cap.
complexity_scope.oracle: Exact scalar component value and derivatives through order p in one complete reply.
complexity_scope.output_and_metric: Any xhat in R^d with ||grad F(xhat)||<=epsilon.
complexity_scope.regime: All positive parameters and n>=1, with separate Delta=0 and L_p=0 cases.
complexity_scope.resource: Complete component p-jet calls; all snapshot, residual endpoint, rejected-trial and verification calls count. Internal global model minimization is permitted without additional oracle charge.
complexity_scope.upper_witness_or_lower_coverage: Upper: full verified Taylor-residual epoch algorithm, Algorithm 1. Lower: unrestricted randomized measurable adaptive algorithms; no span restriction.

evidence.statement_check: Checked exact derivative order, both regularity classes, probability and cap conventions, all-positive regime and boundary cases.

content.intended_use: Match the finite-sum component-count exponent and preserve initialization and boundary regimes.

proofs.locator: Appendix A pp.12–15; Appendices B–D pp.16–22; Appendix E pp.23–24
map: Lemmas A.1–A.2 bound Taylor-residual second moments and maximal gradient-estimation error over an adaptive epoch with conditional failure <=1/64. Snapshot p-jets supply all Taylor corrections; each sampled residual costs two actual component calls.

Lemma A.3 gives boundary-step decrease d0 or interior-step endpoint gradient <=epsilon/2. Algorithm 1 verifies exact endpoint gradient and value; it accepts a nonterminal trial only after m boundary steps and decrease at least m d0.

Proposition A.4 uses H=floor(Delta/(m d0))+1 and 2H trials. Nontermination needs at least H bad trials; conditional failure bounds and Markov give failure <=1/32 without independence of trial outcomes. Each trial costs <=2n+2Bm=O(n); m=ceil(sqrt(n)), B=64m give O_p(S_p).

Appendix B supplies flat gates and dimension-free radial derivative estimates. Lemma C.1 supplies the chain's gap <=2T, unfinished-stage gradient >1/3 and individual pth-derivative Lipschitz bound H_(p+1)/rho, independent of T and D.

Appendix D imports a fixed-table censored-row information bound, stage freshness and exact complete-p-jet truncation. Proposition D.5 leaves an unfinished direction with probability >=95/128 when N<=r_rho J/2 and the stated logarithmic block dimension holds. Tables are fixed before interaction; repeated rows are not fresh samples.

Appendix E scales f_i(y)=alpha R_i(beta y), beta^p=L_p rho/(6H_(p+1)epsilon), alpha=6epsilon/beta and T=floor(c_(T,p)K_p rho^(1/p)). Balancing rho asymptotic to n^(-1/2) gives Omega_p(K_p n^(1-1/(2p))). Appendix E.1 provides Omega(n); E.2 covers small n. Individual inclusion in mean-squared regularity yields the sandwich.

For Delta=0, 0 is stationary. For L_p=0, each component is a degree-at-most-p polynomial recovered by one origin p-jet; n calls determine F. A coercive quadratic perturbation and rational enumeration produce an epsilon-stationary point with no further calls. The hidden-index family supplies the matching lower bound for Delta>0.

assumptions: F(0)-inf_{R^d}F<=Delta<infinity. Only F must be bounded below.
No bounds on lower-order derivative magnitudes, lower-order smoothness or offsets across components.
A query chooses i in [n], x in R^d and returns exactly (f_i(x),grad f_i(x),...,D^p f_i(x)), at cost one.
Query indices, points, stopping and output are arbitrary measurable functions of previous replies and an independent private random tape; internal computation is unrestricted.
statement.conclusion: c_p S_p<=M_p^ind<=M_p^ms<=C_p S_p. If Delta=0, zero queries suffice. If Delta>0 and L_p=0, both complexities are Theta(n). Constants are independent of dimension but need not be uniform for growing p.
statement.objects_and_definitions: F=n^(-1)sum_{i=1}^n f_i on R^d, f_i in C^p, initial point 0. For a k-linear tensor A, ||A||_op=sup_{||h_l||<=1}|A[h_1,...,h_k]|. Individual class: ||D^p f_i(x)-D^p f_i(y)||_op<=L_p||x-y|| for every i,x,y. Mean-squared class: [n^(-1)sum_i||D^p f_i(x)-D^p f_i(y)||_op^2]^(1/2)<=L_p||x-y|| for every x,y. M_p^ind and M_p^ms are the smallest deterministic query caps giving success >=2/3 uniformly over all admissible instances and all finite dimensions. Define K_p=Delta L_p^(1/p)epsilon^(-(p+1)/p), S_p=n+K_p n^(1-1/(2p)).
statement.parameter_domains: Positive Delta,L_p,epsilon, n>=1 and fixed integer p>=2; worst case over all finite d. Boundary statements additionally allow Delta=0 or L_p=0 with epsilon>0.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every fixed integer p>=2 there exist c_p,C_p>0 depending only on p such that the conclusion holds for every n>=1 and positive Delta,L_p,epsilon. The lower bound covers all randomized adaptive algorithms, unbounded queries and unqueried outputs. Upper success is at least 31/32 on every admissible instance with a deterministic cap.
